emily_spt: FYI customer #4432 reporting NXDOMAIN for internal hostname `internal-api.prod.tenant.svc.redwood.local` from app hosts in vpc-0aaaaa after tenant onboarding. Worked yesterday.

raj_net: Can you paste a dig and the hosted zone id they think corresponds?

emily_spt: Dig + aws snippets (sanitized):
``
$ dig internal-api.prod.tenant.svc.redwood.local @172.31.0.2 +short
;; -> (nothing) => NXDOMAIN

$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name tenant.svc.redwood.local
{"HostedZones": [{"Id": "/hostedzone/Z0EXAMPLE","Name": "tenant.svc.redwood.local.","Config": {"PrivateZone": true}}]}

$ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/Z0EXAMPLE
"VPCs": [{"VPCRegion": "us-west-2","VPCId": "vpc-0bbbbb"}]  # only VPC-B
```

emily_spt: Customer says app hosts are in vpc-0aaaaa (VPC-A). Hosted zone only associated to VPC-B after a migration.

raj_net: That explains NXDOMAIN. Private hosted zones only resolve in associated VPCs. Remediation options:
- Associate the hosted zone to VPC-A (cross-account steps if needed)
- If cross-account assoc blocked, use Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint + conditional forwarding from VPC-A to the host account

olivia_eng: Also confirm there's no public record shadowing things. Run `dig +short` and `dig @8.8.8.8` to compare.

emily_spt: Public dig returns the public LB IP (they also expose a public edge), but the app requires internal-only record resolving to private IP.

nate_infra: Cross-account assoc steps (owner account must authorize):
``
# In host account (owner of hosted zone)
aws route53 create-vpc-association-authorization --hosted-zone-id Z0EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0aaaaa

# In tenant/VPC account
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0aaaaa
```
If `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` errors with NotAuthorizedException, the authorization step was not done.

raj_net: Also check for resolver rules/forwarders: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules` and `list-resolver-endpoints`. Could be forwarding to on-prem.

emily_spt: They ran list-resolver-rules: none. They do have network firewall policy denying outbound UDP/TCP 53 to custom endpoints. App subnets block egress to 53.

olivia_eng: For quick debug have them run: `dig @172.31.0.2 internal-api.prod.tenant.svc.redwood.local +tcp +trace` and paste output. If it times out, it's likely firewall.

emily_spt: They ran it and got `connection timed out`. Firewall team confirmed denies to 172.31.0.2 from app subnets.

nate_infra: Short-term fixes:
1) Authorize & associate hosted zone to VPC-A so records resolve natively.
2) If assoc cannot be done immediately, create Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints in host account + conditional forward from VPC-A (will require opening outbound 53 from VPC-A to resolver IPs).

emily_spt: Coordinating cross-account assoc now. Asked hosted-zone owner to run `create-vpc-association-authorization`. Waiting on them.

oncall-bot: Incident runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/private-dns-assoc>

raj_net: Note: if app falls back to public IP, TLS cert CN mismatch will occur. Customer reported cert validation errors when the app resolves to public LB.

olivia_eng: So even if public name exists, the app must resolve internal name to internal IP first to avoid TLS breakage. Ensure internal A record is present and preferred by resolver.

emily_spt: Action items:
- Hosted-zone owner to run `create-vpc-association-authorization` (waiting)
- Customer firewall team to temporarily allow outbound 53 to resolver IPs to verify forwarding approach
- Customer-facing note drafted explaining root cause (hosted zone not associated + egress block) and short-term mitigations

nate_infra: If owner cannot run authorization, escalate to account-ops. I can join call with their network lead if needed.

emily_spt: Will update here once auth is granted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
